what: Hand-read ground truth for the 18 staves the absent-instrument veto refuses with OMR_MOVEMENT_REFERENCE on, over the whole of Beethoven 5 / Litolff (imslp984073, 88 pages, dpi 600).
how: Every system holding a refusal was rendered at the dpi the composition harness ran at (600), the DETECTED staff band of each staff was drawn on the render (probe/box_vetoed.py), and the instrument was read off the print inside that box: the margin label where one is printed, the CLEF and the position in the string block where none is. The alto C-clef staff is the Viola in every system here, which fixes the two treble staves above it as Violin I and Violin II and the bass staff below as the cello/bass staff.
naming_convention: score_2x2.py's: Violin I and Violin II are both the name `Violin`, so `printed` below is the instrument NAME the scorer would want, not the desk.

evidence_tiers.hand_read_page: PRIMARY. A human reading the printed raster. This is not the catalog's `source_kind: page` tier, which is an OMR output of the same raster; it is the standard the choir-grouping and ledger-zone audits in this repo settle candidates by.
evidence_tiers.catalog: CORROBORATION ONLY, and weak: the IMSLP roster for beethoven--symphony-5 (source_kind `catalog`, InstrDetail) ends at the word `strings`, so it attests that the work has a string section and says nothing about staff order.
evidence_tiers.encoding: NOT USED. The mvt-4 reference encoding is on disk and would agree, but nothing here needs it and this keeps the adjudication independent of the artefact the OMR benchmarks score against.

They are here because they set the scale the 18 refusals should be read at: the veto's residual is not acting on a page where everything else is right.
